nodes.text: MD Anderson

MD Anderson is an elegant hospital in a reasonably elegant building. The lobby is empty except for a receptionist who looks like a security guard. A pleasant and attractive black woman intimidating if not so big as to deserve it.
The downstairs is all dark hardwood and glass, stained dark and shining through.

Andy and Terry encounter no one as they wind through the halls, board and disembark elevators. Terry leads him through it all. Sounds if they exist don't register, an odd thing for a hospital, eerily empty, padded to prevent mental and physical injury visiting hours used up except in cases such as theirs.
They arrive in Dad's room. It is large for what it is, looks real nice and new and clean. A television dangling from an odd angle plays video of ducks on a lake or a pond somewhere.
It keeps going so it is apparently a duck channel. Different duck scenes play out, but mostly all takes place in the fall. Colorful, orange brown red serene.
Dad loves ducks. He collects painted wooden decoys and statuettes.

Andy sees him and Andy smiles. Know that his first reaction is to cry instead. Dad is connected to his bed, connected to the wall, his mouth is slack and open, his eyes roll around in sockets too big and hollow, he overlooks can't trace or focus and corrects his line of sight.
He is doped up and still agonizing every breath. He manages a big smile for Andy. It is a variation on his tired smile.

Like if he were staying up late and watching a movie. He'd fall asleep sitting up, his head would fall back and a snore would half make it out before he snapped himself back upright. Then he'd look around and the face he'd make when he recovered that smile was brother to the smile that greeted Andy.
Only his gums are bleeding so very goddamn much his skin is so yellow it looks like urine his chest is gauzed up from where they went in and cauterized his lungs in places.
Janessa is sitting in the corner with Mom. They are close to him but not around him. Their energy seems too far removed from his seeming isolation.
Dad speaks to Andy, his words to Andy.
They are pleasantries and he looks at Andy long and hard while saying them taking his time because he can only speak slowly and it hurts a great big deal just to do so.
They keep holding water up for him to sip on. He makes pained, truly pained noises, weak and strong at the same time. He'd been fighting.
All used up. Except for those eyes, those bloodshot all the way through and then some eyes. Hungry, and livid, they were desperate and sad.

Andy hopes to god he didn't know what's happening. Hoped he didn't recognize these hours as his last few hours on this earth. This one loved the earth itself it was his living heaven, geologist scientist teacher father.
Andy talks and touches him puts a wet cloth on his head. Father looks at son with so much love when he does that. They do that taking turns.
So protective. Not wanting to leave his side. Andy is a flood.
Tears. He can't help. He wants to be strong much stronger than this.
The words out of his mouth are a croak. He can't hold it back he can't be that strong.
Like his sister, Andy's initial reaction is collapse. He can't handle any of it. The sight of him, the smell of him, the certainty of death that surrounds him.
He is shattered and shrunken, stubbles scratches against his touch. His skin is a mess of bruises, sores, odd discolorations he don't know what to make of.
He is an old man but he is not this used up.
He smiles and when he smiles he coughs. His throat is bleeding out and in. He vomits up blood and Andy is there with a rag to wash it up.
The clean rags and the dirty rags. He dab him more runs an ice cube over his lips. He want to be a good son.
He's not a good son. He weeps trying to be silent while doing so, stoic or whatever.
The bucket of blood at Andy's feet. It is quite clear and sloshes syrupy.
Dad turns away, watches the ducks.
On the screen a drake lifts off the water, and the water closes up behind it.
Andy eventually falls asleep on the floor next to the air conditioning unit. This is something he did as a child. He finds the sound, the hum, the constant mechanical breeze soothing.
Someone rocks him gently awake.
Dad isn't doing good. Specialists and doctors are in the room consulting with Mom. She tells them to up the morphine.
They ask if she's aware of the consequences, she tells them she's a respiratory therapist, she knows what will happen next.
Janessa is verbally worrying out loud about her immunizations. Janessa says she has two appointments she has to make. Both are required for her to go to Brazil for a month long geology trip.
Curiously enough, Dad was scheduled to lead a similar field trip before his bloodwork came back bad.

Janessa needs a visa and several vaccinations to ward against Yellow Fever and Yellow Fever's friends. She had them scheduled in LA but has to do them here and now right this minute. A doctor takes her shoulder and says she will take her to go and get that taken care of.
My sister says goodbye to Dad who is less than half aware. He doesn't say bye but he does appear to look at her.

[shot:insert door]As Janessa is walking out the door Dad tries to get up out of the bed, he's confused, his medication is confusing him. Orderlies rush in the room to hold him down, strap him down, sedate him more. They all keep saying he shouldn't be fighting like this.

Janessa flees in almost terror, shocked sober afraid dutiful. She has to get an okay from Mom before she goes, she wants to leave on good terms, she waits for the calm to settle back over the room. There is too much passion, too much energy lingering the air for this to be a death room.
It is too much for her.
